questions.question: According to commercial cinematography standards, what is the standard 180-degree shutter rule when shooting at 24 frames per second (fps)?
options: Set shutter speed to 1/24 second
Set shutter speed to 1/48 or 1/50 second to maintain natural motion blur
Set shutter speed to 1/200 second
Shutter speed is irrelevant when shooting in Log
questions.explanation: The 180-degree shutter rule specifies shutter speed should be double the frame rate (1/50s at 24fps) to reproduce natural human motion cadence.

questions.question: In DaVinci Resolve color grading, which node stage should come before applying a creative look-LUT?
options: Export compression node
Primary balancing, exposure correction, and color space transform
Sharpening and grain overlay
Final audio normalization
questions.explanation: Primary color balance, exposure adjustments, and color space transforms must be normalized into a standard gamut before applying creative aesthetic LUTs.

questions.question: What is the difference between a J-cut and an L-cut in rhythmic video editing?
options: In a J-cut, the audio of the next scene precedes the visual; in an L-cut, the audio of the current scene continues under the next visual
J-cuts are for YouTube, L-cuts are for television
J-cuts require 4K cameras, L-cuts require 1080p
There is no difference; they are synonymous
questions.explanation: A J-cut leads with incoming audio before the video cut; an L-cut lets trailing audio linger while cutting to the following visual shot.

questions.question: What is the target integrated loudness standard for commercial web video on YouTube and Spotify?
options: 0 LUFS
-6 LUFS
-14 LUFS (±1 LUFS)
-30 LUFS
questions.explanation: Standard web audio streaming targets -14 LUFS integrated loudness to prevent harsh digital clipping or automatic volume attenuation.

questions.question: When lighting a human subject with a 3-point setup, what is the function of the backlight (hair light)?
options: To illuminate the camera lens
To separate the subject from the background by creating an edge rim on the hair and shoulders
To eliminate all shadows entirely
To blind the actor for dramatic effect
questions.explanation: The hair light creates specular edge definition, physically separating the subject from the backdrop and enhancing spatial depth.

questions.question: In React 19, which hook is best suited for wrapping expensive state updates so that user typing and clicking interactions remain non-blocking at 60fps?
options: useEffect
useMemo
useTransition
useLayoutEffect
questions.explanation: useTransition allows marking state updates as non-blocking transitions, prioritizing critical user gestures while deferring heavyweight tree updates.

questions.question: When designing a reducer function in modern React or Redux, which of the following is a mandatory contract?
options: It must make asynchronous fetch calls directly
It must be a pure function with no side effects and deterministic return value
It must mutate the incoming state directly to save allocations
It must store state in window.localStorage automatically
questions.explanation: Reducers must always be pure functions: given the same state and action payload, they must return the exact same output with zero side effects.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Context multiplexing (splitting State Context from Dispatch Context)?
options: It increases the bundle size for better compression
Components that only trigger dispatch actions will not re-render when state values update
It automatically saves state to cookies
It converts React components into web components
questions.explanation: By separating State Context from Dispatch Context, child components that only dispatch actions never re-render when state changes.

questions.question: Why should array indices generally be avoided as keys in dynamic React lists?
options: React throws a compile error if an index is used
Indices cause reconciliation bugs and state leakage when items are reordered, inserted, or removed
Index keys disable CSS styles
Index keys make the page reload on click
questions.explanation: Reusing array indices across list mutations breaks React Fiber's identity tracking, causing DOM nodes and local state to bind to the wrong items.

questions.question: In a production Docker container deployment for a Next.js application, why are multi-stage builds recommended?
options: They enable multiple operating systems in one container
They exclude development dependencies and compiler artifacts, minimizing image size and attack surface
They automatically register the domain with DNS
They run unit tests faster in the browser
questions.explanation: Multi-stage Docker builds discard build tools, devDependencies, and raw source files, shipping only the optimized runtime bundle in a secure, compact image.

questions.question: In Meta Ads auction theory, what is the core formula used to determine ad delivery priority?
options: Total Value = Maximum Bid × Account Balance
Total Value = Bid × Estimated Action Rate + User Value (Ad Quality)
Total Value = Daily Budget × Follower Count
Total Value = Click-Through Rate × Website Page Views
questions.explanation: Meta calculates Total Value = Bid × Estimated Action Rate + User Value, rewarding high-relevance creative with lower effective clearing costs.

questions.question: What is the key purpose of Google Tag Manager Server-Side Conversions API (CAPI)?
options: To automatically generate AI marketing videos
To bypass client-side ad blockers and transmission drop-offs by routing conversion events from the cloud server
To increase organic search engine rankings directly
To provide free Google Ad credits
questions.explanation: Server-side CAPI sends hashed user conversion events directly from cloud infrastructure to advertising endpoints, recovering up to 25% of blocked browser events.

questions.question: When scaling dynamic creative testing (DCT), what does the 3:2:2 framework typically refer to?
options: 3 campaigns, 2 ad sets, 2 audiences
3 creatives/videos, 2 primary texts, 2 headlines within one dynamic asset set
3 budgets, 2 conversion goals, 2 pixel IDs
3 days of testing, 2 hours of review, 2 scaling stages
questions.explanation: The 3:2:2 dynamic creative testing methodology pairs 3 videos/visuals with 2 body copy options and 2 headlines to identify algorithmic winners.

questions.question: Why is Blended CAC often preferred alongside Channel-Specific CAC when evaluating omnichannel growth?
options: Blended CAC accounts for cross-channel halo effects and baseline organic conversion velocity
Blended CAC always makes marketing look cheaper
It is required by taxation laws
It eliminates the need to track Google Analytics
questions.explanation: Blended CAC looks at total marketing investment divided by total acquired customers, capturing cross-channel synergy and word-of-mouth effects.

questions.question: What action should be taken when Google Search ad search term reports reveal high spend on irrelevant queries?
options: Increase the daily budget
Add the irrelevant terms to the campaign Negative Keyword list as exact or phrase match
Delete the ad group entirely
Switch to broad match keywords only
questions.explanation: Adding negative keywords eliminates non-converting query traffic and stops wasted ad spend.

questions.question: In Go, what occurs if multiple goroutines send to an unbuffered channel when no receiver is ready?
options: The channel expands dynamically in heap memory
The sending goroutines block until a receiver reads from the channel
A runtime panic is thrown immediately
Messages are dropped silently
questions.explanation: Unbuffered channels have zero capacity; sends block until a corresponding receive is ready.

questions.question: Which Go primitive should be used to wait for a collection of concurrently executed goroutines to finish?
options: sync.Mutex
sync.WaitGroup
atomic.Value
channel select
questions.explanation: sync.WaitGroup provides Add, Done, and Wait methods for coordinating goroutine completion.

questions.question: How should context cancellation be propagated down a call hierarchy in Go microservices?
options: Pass the context.Context as the first parameter to functions
Store context in a package-level global variable
Use OS process signals
Write context to disk
questions.explanation: Idiomatic Go requires passing context.Context explicitly as the first function parameter.

questions.question: In gRPC over HTTP/2, what enables multiplexing multiple concurrent RPC calls over a single TCP connection?
options: HTTP/2 Binary Framing & Streams
TLS Session Tickets
Gzip Compression
Chunked Transfer Encoding
questions.explanation: HTTP/2 breaks messages into binary frames interleaved across independent bidirectional streams on one connection.

title: Creative Direction & Brand Identity Systems Assessment

questions.question: In modern design systems, what is the primary distinction between a global token and an alias/semantic token?
options: Global tokens store raw values (e.g. blue-500); alias tokens assign contextual meaning (e.g. color-primary)
Global tokens only work in CSS; alias tokens only work in Figma
Global tokens cannot be used in dark mode
Alias tokens must always be numbers
questions.explanation: Global tokens define the raw design palette; semantic alias tokens reference global tokens with context and intent.

questions.question: What is the WCAG AA minimum contrast ratio requirement for normal body text against its background?
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.1 AA mandates a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for regular text.

questions.question: Why is a modular typographic scale (e.g. 1.25 Major Third) preferred in scalable brand systems?
options: It provides harmonious, mathematically consistent proportions across all device viewports
It reduces web font download sizes
It eliminates font rendering differences across operating systems
It replaces CSS flexbox
questions.explanation: A modular scale ensures visual harmony and deliberate visual hierarchy across all font sizes.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of columnar storage formats (like Apache Parquet) for analytical queries (OLAP)?
options: Fast random single-row inserts
Column projection and compression skip irrelevant columns, drastically reducing I/O
Automatic human-readable plain text formatting
No schema definition needed
questions.explanation: Columnar storage reads only the columns referenced in the query and yields high compression ratios.

questions.question: In Apache Kafka, how is consumer group horizontal scaling bounded for a given topic?
options: By the number of partitions in the topic
By the number of brokers in the cluster
By CPU core count on the producer
Kafka topics allow unlimited active consumers per partition
questions.explanation: Each partition in a Kafka topic is consumed by at most one consumer instance in a consumer group.

questions.question: What guarantees idempotency in ETL data pipeline stages?
options: Re-running the pipeline on identical input data produces identical results without duplicates or side-effects
The pipeline runs 10x faster on re-execution
The database automatically caches queries
The pipeline requires zero CPU
questions.explanation: Idempotence ensures that retrying failed batches results in the exact same output without data corruption.
